#    THE COWARD KING

# Product Backlog / User Stories

## Tecnológico de Monterrey

**59 User Stories**

| Section 1  Core Mechanics  |

## User Story \#1   Action Points Starting Pool

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | start each horde with 5 Action Points (AP) |
| **So that** | have resources available to play cards from my very first turn |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Player begins every horde with exactly 5 AP. |
| **AC2** | AP counter is visible in the HUD at all times. |
| **AC3** | AP cannot go below zero. |
| **AC4** | Cards requiring more AP than available are visually disabled. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#2   AP Carryover Between Turns

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | accumulate unused AP across turns with no cap |
| **So that** | save resources to deploy powerful multi-card strategies later in the horde |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Unspent AP adds to next turn's pool with no upper limit. |
| **AC2** | Saved AP persists until the end of the horde. |
| **AC3** | HUD displays the updated accumulated AP correctly after each turn. |
| **AC4** | AP resets to 5 at the start of the next horde (plus any bonus). |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#3   AP Bonus on Horde Victory

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | receive \+5 bonus AP after winning a horde |
| **So that** | enter the next horde with a head-start that rewards good play |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | \+5 AP is added to the starting pool of the next horde only. |
| **AC2** | Bonus is shown on the horde transition screen. |
| **AC3** | HUD reflects the bonus correctly from turn 1 of the next horde. |
| **AC4** | Bonus does not stack across multiple horde wins. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 4 hours |

## User Story \#4   King Movement

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | move the King one tile in any of 8 directions per turn |
| **So that** | reposition him strategically to keep enemies away from his safe zone |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Valid adjacent tiles are highlighted when the King is selected. |
| **AC2** | King cannot move to tiles occupied by allies or enemies. |
| **AC3** | Moving the King consumes the player's main action for that turn. |
| **AC4** | The 3x3 safe zone moves together with the King. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#5   Dynamic Safe Zone

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | have the King's 3x3 safe zone always move with him |
| **So that** | maintain consistent protection regardless of where I reposition him |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Safe zone is always centered on the King's current tile. |
| **AC2** | Safe zone updates visually on every King movement. |
| **AC3** | Safe zone is highlighted in a distinct soft-green color on the board. |
| **AC4** | Defeat condition checks are always relative to the current safe zone position. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#6   Playing Cards from Hand

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | spend AP to play one or more cards from my hand in a single turn |
| **So that** | deploy multiple units or traps efficiently when I have enough resources |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Clicking a card highlights valid placement tiles. |
| **AC2** | Multiple cards can be played in one turn if total AP is sufficient. |
| **AC3** | Cards cannot be placed on occupied tiles. |
| **AC4** | Played cards are removed from hand until the next horde. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 2 days |

## User Story \#7   Turn Phase Structure

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | have each turn divided into a clear Player Phase and Enemy Phase |
| **So that** | take my action knowing exactly when enemies will move in response |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Player Phase always resolves before Enemy Phase. |
| **AC2** | During Enemy Phase the player cannot input any action. |
| **AC3** | Current phase is indicated in the HUD. |
| **AC4** | Turn counter increments only after both phases complete. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#8   Enemy Auto-Advance

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | see all enemies advance one tile toward the King during every Enemy Phase |
| **So that** | predict enemy positions and plan defensive placements accordingly |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Every enemy advances exactly 1 tile per turn (Elite Warriors: 2). |
| **AC2** | Enemies take the shortest available path toward the King. |
| **AC3** | Enemy movement is animated so the player can track it. |
| **AC4** | Blocked tiles force enemies to take adjacent detours. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 2 days |

## User Story \#9   Ally Auto-Attack

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | have deployed ally units automatically attack enemies within range each Enemy Phase |
| **So that** | maintain a defensive line without manually triggering each attack |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Each ally attacks the nearest enemy within its defined range every Enemy Phase. |
| **AC2** | Damage is applied correctly according to the ally's DMG stat. |
| **AC3** | Attack animation plays to give clear visual feedback. |
| **AC4** | Allies do not attack if no enemy is in range. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 2 days |

## User Story \#10   End Turn Button

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | click an End Turn button to confirm my phase and trigger the Enemy Phase |
| **So that** | retain explicit control over when my turn ends, even if I take no action |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | End Turn button is always visible during the Player Phase. |
| **AC2** | Clicking it immediately transitions to Enemy Phase resolution. |
| **AC3** | Button is disabled and non-interactive during Enemy Phase. |
| **AC4** | Skipping an action and pressing End Turn is always a valid choice. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 4 hours |

| Section 2   Card System  |

## User Story \#11   Random Hand at Horde Start

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | receive 3 randomly drawn cards from the pool of 15 at the start of each horde |
| **So that** | face a unique strategic challenge every run |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Exactly 3 cards are drawn randomly when a horde starts. |
| **AC2** | No duplicate cards appear in the same 3-card draw. |
| **AC3** | Cards are drawn from the full pool of 15\. |
| **AC4** | Hand is displayed in the Hand Zone at the bottom of the screen. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#12 Card Retention Between Hordes

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | choose 1 card from my previous hand to keep when transitioning to the next horde |
| **So that** | build continuity between encounters and develop multi-horde strategies |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Card retention screen appears after every horde victory. |
| **AC2** | All cards from the previous hand are displayed as selectable options. |
| **AC3** | Player must choose exactly 1 card to retain. |
| **AC4** | Retained card appears in the new hand alongside 3 freshly drawn cards. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

# User Story \#13   Maximum Hand Size of 4

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | hold a maximum of 4 cards at any time |
| **So that** | manage a focused set of tools rather than an overwhelming hand |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Hand never exceeds 4 cards under any circumstance. |
| **AC2** | Hand Zone renders all 4 cards visibly without overlap. |
| **AC3** | Played cards reduce hand size immediately. |
| **AC4** | Hovering over a card shows its full stats in a tooltip. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 4 hours |

## User Story \#14   Knight Card  \[Epic: Attack Units — Story 1 of 4\]

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | play the Knight card (3 AP) to deploy a melee ally that actively hunts the nearest enemy |
| **So that** | have a durable frontline fighter that intercepts threats advancing toward the King |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Knight costs exactly 3 AP to place on any unoccupied tile. |
| **AC2** | Knight has 80 HP and 30 DMG; stats are displayed on the card face. |
| **AC3** | Knight moves 1 tile per turn toward the nearest enemy and attacks when adjacent. |
| **AC4** | Knight is removed from the board when its HP reaches 0\. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#15   Wall Card  \[Epic: Defense Units — Story 1 of 4\]

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | play the Wall card (3 AP) to place an immovable high-HP barrier that blocks a tile |
| **So that** | force enemies to spend turns destroying or routing around it, buying time for other units |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Wall costs exactly 3 AP to place on any unoccupied tile. |
| **AC2** | Wall has 150 HP and 0 DMG; stats are displayed on the card face. |
| **AC3** | Wall is stationary and does not attack; enemies must either destroy it or path around it. |
| **AC4** | Wall is removed from the board when its HP reaches 0\. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 4 hours |

## User Story \#16   Exile Card  \[Epic: Political Cards — Story 1 of 4\]

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | place the Exile card (2 AP) as a hidden trap tile that paralyzes the first enemy to step on it |
| **So that** | neutralize a high-priority threat for 2 turns without spending AP on a combat unit |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Exile costs exactly 2 AP to place on any unoccupied tile. |
| **AC2** | The first enemy that enters the Exile tile is paralyzed and cannot move for exactly 2 turns. |
| **AC3** | Exile is consumed and removed from the board after it triggers once. |
| **AC4** | A visual indicator distinguishes the Exile tile from empty tiles while it is active. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#17   Royal Guard and Decoy Cards

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | use the Royal Guard to absorb one hit for the King and the Decoy to redirect enemy attention |
| **So that** | have last-resort protection tools that can save a run when emergencies arise |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Royal Guard (2 AP, 90 HP) follows the King automatically and absorbs the first enemy hit aimed at him. |
| **AC2** | Decoy (1 AP, 30 HP) causes all enemies to prioritize it over the King while it is alive. |
| **AC3** | Both cards are removed from the board when their HP reaches 0\. |
| **AC4** | Decoy destruction reverts enemy targeting back to the King. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#18   Trench Card

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | place a Trench card to slow all enemies adjacent to that tile |
| **So that** | create chokepoints that buy time for allies to deal damage |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Trench costs 1 AP and has 40 HP and 0 DMG. |
| **AC2** | Any enemy adjacent to the Trench can move only 1 tile every 2 turns. |
| **AC3** | Effect persists as long as the Trench remains on the board. |
| **AC4** | Trench is removed when its HP reaches 0\. |
| **Priority** | 3  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 4 hours |

## User Story \#19   Card AP Cost Display

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | see each card's AP cost displayed prominently on its face in the Hand Zone |
| **So that** | make fast resource decisions without needing to open a details panel |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | AP cost is shown as a number on the top-left corner of each card. |
| **AC2** | Cards with insufficient AP are visually grayed out or disabled. |
| **AC3** | Cost reflects any permanent upgrades applied to that card. |
| **AC4** | Cost is consistent across the Hand Zone, Shop, and hover tooltip. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 4 hours |

## User Story \#20   Card Placement Validation

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | receive clear visual feedback distinguishing valid from invalid placement tiles before I click |
| **So that** | avoid accidental misplacements and plan my deployment confidently |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Valid tiles highlight in a distinct color when a card is selected. |
| **AC2** | Occupied or out-of-range tiles show a different color indicating they are blocked. |
| **AC3** | Feedback updates in real time as the cursor moves. |
| **AC4** | Highlight disappears immediately when selection is cancelled. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#21   Enemy Spawn System

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | see 3 new enemies spawn on the far end of the board each Enemy Phase |
| **So that** | face constant pressure that forces me to keep managing the board actively |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Exactly 3 enemies spawn per Enemy Phase at rows 0 or 7\. |
| **AC2** | Spawn columns are randomized each turn. |
| **AC3** | No two enemies can spawn on the same tile in the same phase. |
| **AC4** | Spawned enemies are immediately registered in the board grid. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 2 days |

## User Story \#22   Skeleton Enemy (Level 1\)

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | face Skeleton enemies with predictable, low-difficulty stats in Level 1 |
| **So that** | learn the core loop before facing tougher enemies in later levels |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Skeletons have 50 HP and deal 15 DMG. |
| **AC2** | Skeletons advance 1 tile per turn toward the King. |
| **AC3** | Skeletons are removed from the board when HP reaches 0\. |
| **AC4** | Skeletons display with their correct sprite distinct from other enemy types. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#23   Ogre Enemy (Level 2\)

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | fight tougher Ogre enemies in Level 2 that require more coordinated defenses |
| **So that** | be forced to use synergy-based card combinations rather than simple placements |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Ogres have 80 HP and deal 25 DMG. |
| **AC2** | Ogres move 1 tile per turn. |
| **AC3** | Ogres require stronger units or multi-card combos to handle efficiently. |
| **AC4** | Ogre sprite is visually distinct from Skeletons and Elite Warriors. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#24   Elite Warrior Enemy (Level 3\)

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | face Elite Warriors in Level 3 who move 2 tiles per turn |
| **So that** | be forced to rethink defensive formations that worked in earlier levels |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Elite Warriors have 100 HP and deal 35 DMG. |
| **AC2** | Elite Warriors move 2 tiles per turn, bypassing slow-movement traps. |
| **AC3** | Their increased speed makes them the most dangerous regular enemy. |
| **AC4** | Elite Warrior sprite is visually distinct from other enemy types. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#25   Boss Summoning Mechanic

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | fight bosses that summon an ally, remain stationary while it lives, and advance 1 tile when it dies |
| **So that** | experience a new layer of challenge that tests how well I can manage the board under pressure |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Boss spawns 1 normal enemy adjacent to itself at combat start. |
| **AC2** | Boss does not move while the summoned ally is alive. |
| **AC3** | Boss advances exactly 1 tile toward the King each time its ally dies. |
| **AC4** | Boss immediately summons a new ally after advancing. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 2 days |

## User Story \#26   Boss Stats per Level

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | face progressively harder bosses across the three levels |
| **So that** | feel a clear difficulty escalation that keeps each level's boss encounter meaningful |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Skeleton King (Level 1): 200 HP / 30 DMG, summons Skeletons. |
| **AC2** | Ogre Boss (Level 2): 350 HP / 40 DMG, summons Ogres. |
| **AC3** | Brave King (Level 3): 500 HP / 50 DMG, summons Elite Warriors. |
| **AC4** | Each boss has a visually distinct sprite from regular enemies. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#27   Horde Victory by Survival

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | win a horde automatically after surviving 30 turns |
| **So that** | have a clear, attainable goal even when I cannot eliminate all enemies |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Turn counter tracks progress toward 30 and is always visible. |
| **AC2** | Victory triggers at the end of turn 30 if no defeat condition has occurred. |
| **AC3** | Card retention screen appears immediately after horde victory. |
| **AC4** | 10 gold is awarded upon winning a horde. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 4 hours |

## User Story \#28   Defeat by King Contact

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | have a clear Game Over triggered the moment an enemy occupies the King's tile |
| **So that** | understand exactly what I am protecting and feel the weight of every enemy advance |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Game Over is triggered the moment any enemy occupies the King's tile. |
| **AC2** | Check occurs after every individual enemy movement step. |
| **AC3** | Game state freezes immediately upon King contact. |
| **AC4** | Game Over screen shows level, horde reached, and gold lost. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 4 hours |

## User Story \#29   Defeat by Safe Zone Breach

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | have a clear Game Over triggered when 2 or more enemies simultaneously occupy the 3x3 safe zone |
| **So that** | understand that clustering enemies near the King is just as fatal as direct contact |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Game Over triggers if 2 or more enemies simultaneously occupy the 3x3 zone. |
| **AC2** | Check occurs after each enemy movement step within the Enemy Phase. |
| **AC3** | Safe zone occupancy is tracked in real time. |
| **AC4** | Defeat screen is identical to the King-contact screen. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 4 hours |

## User Story \#30   Turn Counter in HUD

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | see the current turn out of 30 displayed in the HUD at all times |
| **So that** | make time-sensitive decisions knowing exactly how many turns remain |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Counter displays as 'Turn X / 30' in the HUD. |
| **AC2** | Counter increments at the end of each full turn cycle. |
| **AC3** | Counter resets to 1 at the start of each new horde. |
| **AC4** | Counter is always visible alongside AP, gold, level, and horde info. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 4 hours |

## User Story \#31   Gold Income per Horde

| User Story \#31   Gold Income per Horde |  |
| :---- | :---- |

## User Story \#32   Gold Loss on Death

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | lose all unspent gold when the King dies |
| **So that** | feel pressure to spend wisely, knowing that hoarding gold carries real risk |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | All unspent gold is removed on death. |
| **AC2** | Purchased upgrades are always retained regardless of death. |
| **AC3** | Gold loss amount is displayed on the Game Over screen. |
| **AC4** | Gold counter resets to 0 when the player restarts from the checkpoint. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 4 hours |

## 

## User Story \#33   Permanent Card Upgrades

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | spend gold to permanently upgrade cards between hordes |
| **So that** | feel long-term improvement that makes each new attempt stronger than the last |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Upgrades are purchased via the Upgrade / Shop Screen between hordes. |
| **AC2** | Each upgrade costs 20–50 gold depending on its power. |
| **AC3** | Upgrades persist after death and across all future runs. |
| **AC4** | Upgraded stats are reflected on the card face immediately. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 2 days |

## User Story \#34   Checkpoint System Per Level

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | restart from Horde 1 of the current level when the King dies |
| **So that** | feel that failure is fair and never lose more progress than one level's worth of work |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Death in Level 2 Horde 3 returns to Level 2 Horde 1, not Level 1\. |
| **AC2** | Checkpoint is set automatically when starting a new level. |
| **AC3** | Game Over screen explains the checkpoint behavior clearly. |
| **AC4** | Player cannot manually select a starting level; progression is always sequential. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#35   Auto-Save After Level Completion

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | have the game auto-save when I complete all 3 hordes and the boss of a level |
| **So that** | close the game and resume from my last completed level without losing progress |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Auto-save triggers after defeating the boss of each level. |
| **AC2** | Save stores: current level index, gold balance, and all purchased upgrades. |
| **AC3** | Resume option on the main menu loads the last auto-save correctly. |
| **AC4** | No manual save option is required. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |

## User Story \#36   Level Progression: 3 Hordes \+ 1 Boss

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | progress through exactly 3 regular hordes followed by 1 boss fight within each level |
| **So that** | experience a structured difficulty ramp within every level |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Each level contains exactly 3 horde encounters and 1 boss fight. |
| **AC2** | Boss encounter unlocks only after all 3 hordes of that level are defeated. |
| **AC3** | Total encounters across the full game equal 12\. |
| **AC4** | Level and horde indicator in the HUD reflects the current encounter accurately. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | see the 8x8 board centered on screen with the Hand Zone below and HUD above |
| **So that** | have all critical information visible without opening any sub-menus |

## User Story \#39   Game Over Screen

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | see a Game Over screen that shows my progress and lets me retry or quit |
| **So that** | quickly understand what I lost and decide my next action without frustration |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Screen displays: level reached, horde reached, gold lost, upgrades retained. |
| **AC2** | Two options are shown: Retry from Horde 1 of current level, Return to Main Menu. |
| **AC3** | Screen is triggered by both defeat conditions. |
| **AC4** | Retained upgrades are listed to soften the loss. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#40   Horde Transition Screen

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | see a transition screen between hordes where I select 1 card to retain |
| **So that** | make a meaningful deck-building decision that shapes my next encounter strategy |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Screen appears automatically after every horde victory. |

## User Story \#45   Board Grid Data Model  \[Engineering Backlog\]

| As | engineering team |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | define and implement the Board component as an 8x8 grid\[row\]\[col\] data structure with a single-occupancy rule per tile |
| **So that** | provide a reliable, queryable spatial model that all game systems (placement, pathfinding, safe zone, defeat detection) can depend on without duplication or inconsistency |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Board exposes placeObject(obj, row, col), removeObject(row, col), getObject(row, col), and isTileEmpty(row, col) as its public API; no other system modifies grid state directly. |
| **AC2** | placeObject() throws a descriptive error and makes no state change if the target tile is occupied or out of bounds. |
| **AC3** | Board state is updated synchronously so that any read immediately after a write reflects the new state. |
| **AC4** | All internal coordinates use a consistent (row: 0–7, col: 0–7) convention; no magic index arithmetic appears outside the Board class. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 2 days |

## User Story \#46   Core Class Hierarchy  \[Engineering Backlog\]

| User Story \#46   Core Class Hierarchy  \[Engineering Backlog\] |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **As** | engineering team |
| **I want** | define and implement the full class hierarchy — GameObject, Unit, Card, Board, TurnManager, HandSystem, and EnemySpawner — with clearly specified interfaces before any feature work begins |
| **So that** | ensure every developer on the team works against stable, well-documented contracts so that parallel feature development does not produce conflicting or redundant logic |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | GameObject is the base class for all entities; it exposes position, type, isActive, update(), render(), and interact() — no derived class bypasses these. |
| **AC2** | Unit (extends GameObject) adds HP, DMG, speed, move(), attack(), and takeDamage(amount); all combat entities extend Unit and override only what differs. |
| **AC3** | Card (extends GameObject) adds cost, name, cardType, activate(targetTile), and getValidTiles(); all 15 card implementations extend Card with no duplicated placement logic. |
| **AC4** | TurnManager, HandSystem, and EnemySpawner are documented with their public method signatures and responsibilities in the codebase before implementation; any cross-system call goes through these interfaces only. |
| **Priority** | 1  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 3 days |

## User Story \#47   Enemy Navigation Around Obstacles

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | see enemies intelligently navigate around walls, allies, and other obstacles to always reach the King |
| **So that** | face threats that feel relentless and smart, so that placing a Wall or Guardian creates a meaningful tactical decision rather than a permanent blocker |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | Every enemy resolves its movement by taking the shortest available path to the King's current tile each Enemy Phase; paths update dynamically if the King moves or obstacles change. |
| **AC2** | When the direct path is blocked by a Wall, ally, or other enemy, the unit selects the shortest unobstructed adjacent route; it never skips its turn due to a blocked path. |
| **AC3** | Elite Warriors apply the same pathfinding logic but advance 2 tiles per resolution step, consuming two path nodes per Enemy Phase. |
| **AC4** | Pathfinding produces no out-of-bounds accesses, no infinite loops, and completes within a single frame for all ≤ 24 simultaneously active enemies (3 enemies × 8 turns max on board). |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 3 days |

## User Story \#48   Run Persistence Across Sessions

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | be able to close the game at any time and return later to find my checkpoint, gold balance, and purchased upgrades exactly as I left them |
| **So that** | play in short sessions without fear of losing hard-earned progress, reinforcing the roguelite loop rather than undermining it |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | The game writes a save file automatically upon completing each level (after the boss is defeated); no manual save action is required from the player. |
| **AC2** | The save file stores: current level index (1–3), current gold balance, and the full list of purchased card upgrades with their stat values. |
| **AC3** | On launch, if a valid save file exists, the Resume option on the main menu loads the player directly to Horde 1 of their saved level with all upgrades applied. |
| **AC4** | If the save file is missing, empty, or structurally invalid, the game falls back to a default new-game state and logs a descriptive error; it does not crash or display a blank screen. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 2 days |

## User Story \#49   Mouse-Driven Controls

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | control the entire game exclusively with the mouse |
| **So that** | enjoy an accessible and intuitive control scheme with no keyboard input required |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | All gameplay actions — card selection, tile placement, King movement, End Turn, and menu navigation — are performed via left-click only. |
| **AC2** | Right-click or clicking any non-interactive area cancels the current selection without modifying game state. |
| **AC3** | No keyboard input is required at any point during a horde; the game is fully playable with mouse alone. |
| **AC4** | The cursor changes to a contextual icon (pointer, crosshair, or cancel) to communicate the current interaction state before the player clicks. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | 1 day |

## User Story \#50   Gameplay Performance Targets

| As | player |
| :---- | :---- |
| **I want** | experience smooth, uninterrupted gameplay throughout every horde and Enemy Phase |
| **So that** | focus entirely on tactical decisions without stutters or freezes breaking my concentration |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **AC1** | The game renders at a stable 60 FPS during all Player Phase interactions (card hover, tile highlight, King movement preview) on a machine with an Intel Core i5 (8th gen or equivalent) CPU and 8 GB RAM. |
| **AC2** | Enemy Phase resolution — including movement of up to 24 simultaneous units, pathfinding recalculation, auto-attack damage application, and board re-render — completes in ≤ 500 ms per turn on the same reference hardware. |
| **AC3** | The board renders all 64 tiles, up to 24 enemy units, up to 8 ally units, and all active political card zones simultaneously with no dropped frames, as verified by running the worst-case board state in a manual test. |
| **AC4** | No memory leak causes the frame rate to degrade by more than 5 FPS over the course of a full 30-turn horde, as measured by profiling tool output. |
| **Priority** | 2  (1 \= highest) |
| **Estimation** | Ongoing |

## **Functional and Non-Functional Requirements Classification**

The product backlog was filtered into functional and non-functional requirements according to SCRUM methodology. Functional requirements describe the gameplay, UI, progression, enemy, card, and user-facing systems of the game. Non-functional and technical requirements describe system quality attributes such as architecture, persistence, usability, performance, and maintainability.

Functional Requirements:

User Stories \#1–\#44, \#47, \#49, \#51–\#59

Non-Functional / Technical Requirements:

User Stories \#45, \#46, \#48, \#50

Hybrid Requirements:

User Story \#47 — Enemy Navigation Around Obstacles

User Story \#49 — Mouse-Driven Controls

## 6\. UML Use Case Diagrams

The following UML use case diagrams represent the main interactions between external actors and the proposed system for The Coward King. The diagrams are divided into three areas: core gameplay, progression and persistence, and web/database support. This separation helps keep each diagram clear and focused on a specific part of the system.

## 6.1 Core Gameplay Use Case Diagram

![][image1]

This diagram shows the main gameplay interactions between the player and the core gameplay systems of The Coward King. The player can start the game, view the main menu, move the King, play cards, end the turn, view the HUD, survive hordes, fight bosses, retain cards, and experience game over or victory outcomes. The diagram also includes the Enemy AI System, which is responsible for enemy spawning and enemy advancement toward the King. The include and extend relationships show how some actions depend on or lead to other gameplay events, such as ending the turn triggering enemy advancement, enemy advancement including combat resolution, and safe zone breaches potentially leading to the Game Over screen.

## 6.2 Progression and Persistence Use Case Diagram

![][image2]

This diagram represents the progression and persistence mechanics of The Coward King. The player can earn gold, purchase card upgrades, resume a saved game, and restart from a checkpoint. The Save System is included as a secondary actor because it handles save-related responsibilities such as auto-saving progress, loading saved progress, and validating save files. This diagram focuses on the systems that allow the player to maintain progress across game sessions and continue developing their run through gold, upgrades, checkpoints, and saved data.

## 6.3 Web and Database Support Use Case Diagram

![][image3]  
This diagram describes the web and database support interactions related to The Coward King. Visitors can view the game overview, rules, instructions, and credits. Players can access the game, view their stats, and view the leaderboard. Admin users can manage web content, manage users, view analytics, and update game data. The Authenticate User use case is included for actions that require verified access, such as accessing player-specific information or performing admin-level actions. This diagram helps show how the external web platform supports the game through information access, user interaction, and administrative control.

| UC\_Advance  —  Advance Toward King |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_Advance |
| Use Case Name | Advance Toward King |
| Actor(s) | Enemy AI |
| Trigger | Enemy Phase resolves after spawning |
| Preconditions | At least one enemy is active on the board |
| Postconditions | All enemies move 1 tile (Elite Warriors 2 tiles) toward the King via shortest path |
| Main Flow | 1\. System iterates over all active enemies. 2\. Each enemy calculates shortest path to King. 3\. Enemy moves 1 tile (or 2 for Elite Warriors). 4\. Combat resolves if enemy is adjacent to an ally. 5\. Safe zone breach is checked after each step. |
| Alternative Flow | If direct path is blocked, enemy takes shortest available detour. |
| Exceptions | If pathfinding finds no valid route, enemy holds position and logs warning. |

 

**Resolve Combat**

| UC\_Combat  —  Resolve Combat |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_Combat |
| Use Case Name | Resolve Combat |
| Actor(s) | Enemy AI |
| Trigger | An enemy moves adjacent to an ally unit |
| Preconditions | An enemy and ally occupy adjacent tiles |
| Postconditions | Damage is applied to both units; units with 0 HP are removed from board |
| Main Flow | 1\. Enemy enters range of ally. 2\. Ally auto-attacks nearest enemy within range. 3\. Damage is applied according to each unit's DMG stat. 4\. Attack animations play. 5\. Units with 0 HP are removed from board. |
| Alternative Flow | If no enemy is within ally range, ally does not attack. |
| Exceptions | If damage calculation produces a negative value, it is clamped to 0\. |

 

**Check Safe Zone Breach**

| UC\_SafeBreach  —  Check Safe Zone Breach |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_SafeBreach |
| Use Case Name | Check Safe Zone Breach |
| Actor(s) | Game System (internal) |
| Trigger | After each enemy movement step during Enemy Phase |
| Preconditions | Enemy Phase is resolving; safe zone coordinates are current |
| Postconditions | If 2+ enemies occupy the safe zone simultaneously, Game Over is triggered |
| Main Flow | 1\. System counts enemies currently inside the 3x3 safe zone. 2\. If count \>= 2, defeat condition is triggered. 3\. Game Over screen is displayed. |
| Alternative Flow | If count is 0 or 1, no action is taken and Enemy Phase continues. |
| Exceptions | If safe zone coordinates are stale, system recalculates before checking. |

 

 

# **Section 2 — Progression & Persistence**

**Earn Gold**

| UC\_EarnGold  —  Earn Gold |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_EarnGold |
| Use Case Name | Earn Gold |
| Actor(s) | Player |
| Trigger | Player wins a horde or boss encounter |
| Preconditions | Player has successfully completed a horde or boss fight |
| Postconditions | 10 gold is added to the player's current gold balance |
| Main Flow | 1\. Horde or boss victory is confirmed. 2\. System adds 10 gold to player's balance. 3\. Gold total is shown on horde transition screen. 4\. HUD updates to reflect new gold amount. |
| Alternative Flow | None. |
| Exceptions | If gold fails to persist after victory, system retries and logs error. |

 

**Lose Gold on Death**

| UC\_LoseGold  —  Lose Gold on Death |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_LoseGold |
| Use Case Name | Lose Gold on Death |
| Actor(s) | Player |
| Trigger | King dies triggering a Game Over |
| Preconditions | Player has unspent gold; a defeat condition has been met |
| Postconditions | All unspent gold is removed; purchased upgrades are retained |
| Main Flow | 1\. Defeat condition triggers. 2\. System records gold lost for Game Over screen. 3\. System sets gold balance to 0\. 4\. Purchased upgrades remain unaffected. 5\. Game Over screen displays gold lost. |
| Alternative Flow | None. |
| Exceptions | If gold reset fails, system forces gold to 0 on next session load. |

 

**Purchase Card Upgrade**

| UC\_PurchaseUpgrade  —  Purchase Card Upgrade |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_PurchaseUpgrade |
| Use Case Name | Purchase Card Upgrade |
| Actor(s) | Player |
| Trigger | Player selects and confirms an upgrade in the Upgrade Shop |
| Preconditions | Player has sufficient gold; upgrade has not been purchased yet |
| Postconditions | Upgrade is applied permanently; gold is deducted; card stats update immediately |
| Main Flow | 1\. Player opens Upgrade Shop between hordes. 2\. System displays all 15 cards with available upgrades and costs. 3\. Player selects an upgrade and confirms purchase. 4\. System deducts gold cost. 5\. Upgrade is applied permanently to the card. 6\. Card face updates to reflect new stats. |
| Alternative Flow | If player lacks sufficient gold, upgrade is grayed out and unselectable. |
| Exceptions | If upgrade fails to save, system rolls back gold deduction and notifies player. |

 

**Restart from Checkpoint**

| UC\_Checkpoint  —  Restart from Checkpoint |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_Checkpoint |
| Use Case Name | Restart from Checkpoint |
| Actor(s) | Player |
| Trigger | Player selects Retry on the Game Over screen |
| Preconditions | A defeat condition has been met; checkpoint is set to Horde 1 of current level |
| Postconditions | Game restarts at Horde 1 of the level where the player died; upgrades are retained; gold resets to 0 |
| Main Flow | 1\. Player clicks Retry on Game Over screen. 2\. System loads checkpoint: Horde 1 of current level. 3\. Gold balance resets to 0\. 4\. All purchased upgrades are applied. 5\. New 3-card hand is drawn. 6\. Board initializes and Player Phase begins. |
| Alternative Flow | If player selects Main Menu instead, no checkpoint is loaded. |
| Exceptions | If checkpoint data is corrupt, system falls back to Level 1 Horde 1 and logs error. |

 

**Auto-Save Progress**

| UC\_AutoSave  —  Auto-Save Progress |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_AutoSave |
| Use Case Name | Auto-Save Progress |
| Actor(s) | Save System |
| Trigger | Player defeats the boss of a level |
| Preconditions | Boss of current level has been defeated |
| Postconditions | Save file is written with current level index, gold balance, and all purchased upgrades |
| Main Flow | 1\. Boss defeat is confirmed. 2\. System collects current level index, gold balance, and upgrade list. 3\. System writes save file. 4\. Save System validates the written file. 5\. Resume option on Main Menu becomes available. |
| Alternative Flow | None — auto-save triggers automatically with no player action required. |
| Exceptions | If save write fails, system retries once and logs error; player is notified. |

 

**Load Saved Progress**

| UC\_LoadSave  —  Load Saved Progress |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_LoadSave |
| Use Case Name | Load Saved Progress |
| Actor(s) | Save System |
| Trigger | Player selects Resume on the Main Menu |
| Preconditions | A valid save file exists on disk |
| Postconditions | Game loads at Horde 1 of the saved level with all upgrades applied |
| Main Flow | 1\. Player clicks Resume. 2\. System locates save file. 3\. Save file is validated (UC\_ValidateSave). 4\. System reads level index, gold balance, and upgrade list. 5\. Game initializes with loaded state. 6\. Board displays and Player Phase begins. |
| Alternative Flow | None. |
| Exceptions | If save file is missing or invalid, system falls back to new-game state and logs error. |

 

**Resume Game**

| UC\_Resume  —  Resume Game |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_Resume |
| Use Case Name | Resume Game |
| Actor(s) | Player |
| Trigger | Player clicks Resume on the Main Menu |
| Preconditions | A valid save file exists; Resume option is not grayed out |
| Postconditions | Player continues from Horde 1 of their last completed level with all upgrades intact |
| Main Flow | 1\. Player clicks Resume. 2\. System triggers UC\_LoadSave. 3\. Save file is loaded and validated. 4\. Game state is restored. 5\. Player Phase begins at saved level. |
| Alternative Flow | If no save file exists, Resume is grayed out and cannot be clicked. |
| Exceptions | If load fails, system returns to Main Menu and displays an error message. |

 

**Validate Save File**

| UC\_ValidateSave  —  Validate Save File |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_ValidateSave |
| Use Case Name | Validate Save File |
| Actor(s) | Save System |
| Trigger | Called during UC\_LoadSave or UC\_AutoSave |
| Preconditions | A save file exists or has just been written |
| Postconditions | Save file is confirmed valid; or fallback to new-game state is triggered |
| Main Flow | 1\. System reads save file structure. 2\. System checks for required fields: level index, gold balance, upgrade list. 3\. System verifies field types and value ranges. 4\. If valid, returns parsed save data. 5\. If invalid, logs error and triggers fallback. |
| Alternative Flow | None. |
| Exceptions | If file is structurally malformed, system discards it and starts new game without crashing. |

   
 

# **Section 3 — Web & Database Support**

**View Game Overview**

| Exceptions | If page fails to load, system shows a generic error page. |

| Trigger | Visitor clicks on Rules or How to Play section |
| Preconditions | Web platform is online |
| Postconditions | Visitor reads full game rules and instructions |
| Main Flow | 1\. Visitor clicks Rules link. 2\. System displays rules page with AP system, turn structure, card descriptions, win/lose conditions. 3\. Visitor reads content. |
| Alternative Flow | None. |

| Postconditions | Visitor reads team member names and project attributions |

| Alternative Flow | None. |
| Exceptions | None expected. |

 

**Access Game**

| Postconditions | Game loads in browser or redirects to downloadable build |

| Alternative Flow | If user is a Visitor without account, game may load in guest mode. |
| Exceptions | If game build fails to load, system displays error and retry option. |

 

**View Player Stats**

| UC\_ViewStats  —  View Player Stats |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_ViewStats |
| Use Case Name | View Player Stats |
| Actor(s) | Player |
| Trigger | Player clicks on Stats section while logged in |
| Preconditions | Player is authenticated; stats have been recorded from previous sessions |
| Postconditions | Player views personal gameplay statistics |
| Main Flow | 1\. Player clicks Stats. 2\. System authenticates player (UC\_Authenticate). 3\. System retrieves player stats from database. 4\. Stats page displays runs completed, enemies defeated, gold earned, upgrades purchased. |
| Alternative Flow | If no stats exist yet, system shows empty state with prompts to play. |
| Exceptions | If database is unreachable, system shows cached stats or error message. |

 

**View Leaderboard**

| UC\_ViewLeaderboard  —  View Leaderboard |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_ViewLeaderboard |
| Use Case Name | View Leaderboard |
| Actor(s) | Player |
| Trigger | Player clicks on Leaderboard section |
| Preconditions | Player is logged in; leaderboard data exists in the database |
| Postconditions | Player views ranked list of top performers |
| Main Flow | 1\. Player clicks Leaderboard. 2\. System retrieves stored player stats (UC\_StoreStats). 3\. System ranks players by selected metric (e.g., hordes survived). 4\. Leaderboard is displayed with player names and scores. |
| Alternative Flow | If player is not ranked yet, their row is shown at the bottom with current stats. |
| Exceptions | If database query fails, system displays last cached leaderboard with timestamp. |

| Postconditions | Web content (overview, rules, credits) is updated and published |
| Main Flow | 1\. Admin logs in. 2\. Admin navigates to Content Management section. 3\. Admin edits text, images, or links. 4\. Admin publishes changes. 5\. System updates the live web pages. |
| Alternative Flow | Admin may save a draft before publishing. |
| Exceptions | If publish fails, system rolls back and notifies admin. |

 

**Manage Users**

| Trigger | Admin navigates to User Management section |
| Preconditions | Admin is authenticated (UC\_Authenticate) |
| Postconditions | Admin has viewed, edited, or removed user accounts as needed |
| Main Flow | 1\. Admin opens User Management. 2\. System authenticates admin (UC\_Authenticate). 3\. System displays user list with roles and activity. 4\. Admin selects a user to view, edit role, or deactivate account. 5\. Changes are saved to database. |
| Alternative Flow | Admin may filter users by role or activity status. |
| Exceptions | If user deletion fails due to active session, system notifies admin and cancels operation. |

 

**View Analytics**

| UC\_ViewAnalytics  —  View Analytics |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_ViewAnalytics |
| Use Case Name | View Analytics |
| Actor(s) | Admin |
| Trigger | Admin navigates to Analytics dashboard |
| Preconditions | Admin is authenticated; usage data has been collected |
| Postconditions | Admin views aggregated platform metrics |
| Main Flow | 1\. Admin opens Analytics section. 2\. System retrieves aggregated data: active users, games played, most used cards, average horde survival. 3\. Dashboard displays charts and summary stats. |
| Alternative Flow | Admin may filter by date range. |
| Exceptions | If analytics service is unavailable, system displays last known snapshot with timestamp. |

 

**Update Game Data**

| UC\_UpdateGameData  —  Update Game Data |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_UpdateGameData |
| Use Case Name | Update Game Data |
| Actor(s) | Admin |
| Trigger | Admin modifies game configuration data (card stats, enemy stats, level parameters) |
| Preconditions | Admin is authenticated (UC\_Authenticate); game data schema is defined |
| Postconditions | Updated game data is stored and reflected in the live game on next load |
| Main Flow | 1\. Admin opens Game Data Management. 2\. System authenticates admin (UC\_Authenticate). 3\. Admin selects data category (cards, enemies, levels). 4\. Admin modifies values. 5\. System validates changes against schema. 6\. Changes are saved and published to game database. |
| Alternative Flow | Admin may preview changes before publishing. |
| Exceptions | If validation fails, system highlights invalid fields and prevents save. |

 

**Store Player Stats**

| UC\_StoreStats  —  Store Player Stats |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_StoreStats |
| Use Case Name | Store Player Stats |
| Actor(s) | Save System |
| Trigger | Player completes a horde, dies, or finishes a run |
| Preconditions | A gameplay session event has concluded |
| Postconditions | Player stats are persisted in the database for leaderboard and personal stats display |
| Main Flow | 1\. Gameplay event concludes (horde won, death, or victory). 2\. System collects stat data: hordes survived, enemies defeated, gold earned, upgrades purchased. 3\. System writes stats to player record in database. 4\. Leaderboard rankings are recalculated. |
| Alternative Flow | If player is in guest mode, stats are stored locally only. |
| Exceptions | If database write fails, system queues stat update and retries on next connection. |

 

**Authenticate User**

| UC\_Authenticate  —  Authenticate User |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| Use Case ID | UC\_Authenticate |
| Use Case Name | Authenticate User |
| Actor(s) | Player, Admin |
| Trigger | User attempts to access a protected feature (stats, leaderboard, admin panel) |
| Preconditions | User has an account; authentication service is online |
| Postconditions | User is granted or denied access based on credentials and role |
| Main Flow | 1\. User attempts to access protected feature. 2\. System redirects to login screen if not authenticated. 3\. User enters credentials. 4\. System validates credentials against user database. 5\. On success, session token is issued and user accesses feature. |
| Alternative Flow | If user has no account, system offers registration option. |
| Exceptions | If authentication service is down, system denies access and displays maintenance message. |
